newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: FULL TEXT - Westpac/Bank of Melbourne agreed merger.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT - Westpac/Bank of Melbourne agreed merger.

text.p: The following statement was issued by Westpac Banking Corp on Thursday on the agreed A$1.435 billion plan for it to merge with Bank of Melbourne Ltd.

"Westpac Banking Corporation today announced agreement with Bank of Melbourne under which Westpac will make an offer to acquire all the issued shares in Bank of Melbourne through schemes of arrangement.

Under the schemes of arrangement, Bank of Melbourne shareholders will be offered A$$9.75 for each ordinary share and A$15.36 for each convertible preference share. Westpac's offer has a maximum value of $1,435 million for all of Bank of Melbourne's ordinary, convertible preference and partly paid shares.
Westpac's Managing Director Mr Robert Joss said, "This announcement is a significant milestone related to our aim of being the best in Australia and New Zealand.
This merger reinforces our regional approach and takes the bank well down a path where we now have critical share in each of our major customer markets.
"The merged bank will combine Bank of Melbourne's excellent marketing and customer service delivery with Westpac's capabilities in processing, broader product range and credit standing.
"The merger is a partnership for growth of our business in Victoria. Together we will be creating a new competitive force in this important market.
"Our regional banking approach will ensure Bank of Melbourne becomes a stronger competitive force in Victoria and retains its local identity.

"This approach which was established in Western Australia and New Zealand will provide the framework for Victoria in delivering local product and marketing discretion, local credit decision making within Westpac's overall credit policy guidelines, local personnel management and local community sponsorship.
"We will have a local chief executive heading Bank of Melborne.
"The Bank of Melbourne brand will be used throughout Victoria for the combined retail, small business and commercial operations," said Mr Joss.
"Westpac's leading brand name in the corporate and institutional markets will continue in the non-retail market wing the successful formula applied in Western Australia.
"This merger offers benefits to existing Bank of Melbourne customers through a truly national network. It's the best of both worlds.
"Better local servicing which Bank of Melbourne does well and our expertise in product range, technology, and financial markets.
"Both Westpac and Bank of Melbourne customers will also have access to a more extensive distribution network - the combined strength of branches, banking centres, ATMs and telephone banking.
"Customers using branch facilities will benefit because of the larger number of points of representation in the combined network.
"Westpac's non-branch customer access points such as our telephone, banking service and the extensive ATM network will make banking services far more, accessible for everyone," said Mr Joss.
"Our track record with the Challenge Bank integration shows we can deliver mergers with minimal staff losses by successfully using natural attrition during the integration process."

Westpac's Chairman, Mr John Uhrig, announced that Bank of Melbourne's current Chairman, Mr Chris Stewart, will be invited to join the Westpac; Board and also continue to serve as Chairman of the Bank of Melbourne Board.

Bank of Melbourne's ordinary shareholders will receive value equivalent to A$9.75 per share composed of a fully franked special dividend of A$0.90 per share, and either A$8.85 in cash or one Westpac ordinary share plus a maximum of A$1.85 in cash. To the extent that the Westpac average share price exceeds $8.85 over the price setting period, no cash will be payable and an adjustment will be made to the number of Westpac shares issued.
Bank of Melbourne converting preference shareholders will be offered either A$15.36 in cash or two Westpac ordinary shares plus a maximum of A$1.36 cash.
To the extent that the Westpac average share price exceeds A$7.68 over the price setting period, no cash will be payable and an adjustment will be made to the number of Westpac shares issued.

The offer for 100% of the share capital of Bank of Melbourne is subject to approvals from the Federal Treasurer, Australian Competition and Consumer Commission, Reserve Bank of Australia and Bank of Melbourne's ordinary shareholders."
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
